_readme: SINGLE SOURCE OF TRUTH for the corpus of real Chrome extensions Orbit's
live-engine suite loads.
Fixtures encode the fixture author's assumptions, so they pass against
whatever subset of an API happens to exist. Real extensions encode
reality: this corpus is the layer that catches 'every binding is present
and the extension still does nothing'. See refs/EXTENSION_CONFORMANCE.md
section 7.5.
Scripts/extension-corpus status        what is pinned, present and verified
Scripts/extension-corpus fetch         download + verify + unpack every pin
Scripts/extension-corpus fetch vimium  just one, by id or by name
Scripts/extension-corpus verify        re-hash what is on disk against the pins
Scripts/extension-corpus pin           move the pins to the current store version
`fetch` downloads the pinned CRX from the Chrome Web Store update service
with exactly the request Orbit's own ChromeWebStoreClient builds, verifies
the SHA-256 and fails closed on a mismatch -- it never unpacks unverified
code -- then unpacks into ThirdParty/extension-corpus/<id>-<version>/.
ThirdParty/* is gitignored, so nothing large is committed and a fresh
clone rebuilds the corpus from this file.
Pins move only when someone runs `pin`, never as a side effect of
`fetch`. An extension that silently updates underneath the suite turns it
into a flake generator, and the whole point of a corpus entry is that its
expectation was verified against that exact build.
`prodversion` on the download request comes from Chromium/chromium-version.json,
so bumping Chromium changes which build the store serves; re-run `pin`
after a Chromium bump if a fetch starts returning a different version.

extensions.name: Wappalyzer
extensions.exercises: content script, web-accessible resources, page-world globals, cookies, tabs, webRequest, storage, popup, _locales, options_ui
extensions.expectation: on a page carrying a generator meta tag and a page-world window.jQuery, the popup lists both technologies by name
extensions.driver_note: RealWappalyzerLiveTests.swift predates this manifest and loads Wappalyzer from a /private/tmp staging directory, not from ThirdParty/extension-corpus, so this pin currently verifies nothing for it. Recorded as an enforced exception in ExtensionCorpusCoverageGuardTests.unpinnedDriverExceptions.

extensions.name: uBlock Origin Lite
extensions.exercises: declarativeNetRequest static rulesets, updateEnabledRulesets, MV3 service worker
extensions.expectation: a request the enabled ruleset blocks never reaches LiveHTTPTestServer, while a control request does

extensions.name: uBlock Origin
extensions.exercises: MV2 background page, blocking webRequest, WebSocket filtering
extensions.expectation: same server-side oracle as the Lite entry; the WebSocket case is an expected failure recorded in ExpectedAPIGaps.json until WebSocket filtering lands

extensions.name: Dark Reader
extensions.exercises: content script CSS injection, storage.sync, runtime messaging
extensions.expectation: the computed background-color of a white test page becomes dark

extensions.name: Vimium
extensions.exercises: popup-less action, commands, tabs, content scripts, keyboard handling
extensions.expectation: pressing j scrolls the page and the toolbar icon exists

extensions.name: Privacy Badger
extensions.exercises: webRequest observation, storage, privacy, heuristic third-party tracking state
extensions.expectation: its popup, opened through the production toolbar path on a real tab, reaches a terminal state rendered from its own service worker's getPopupData answer
extensions.unreached_expectation: after three visits carrying the same third-party tracker, the tracker is listed in its popup
extensions.blocked_by: LiveHTTPTestServer binds 127.0.0.1 only, so it cannot serve three first-party sites with distinct eTLD+1s and Privacy Badger's heuristic never sees a third party. Needs a host-resolver-rules mapping or a second loopback hostname before the tracker assertion is meaningful.

extensions.name: Stylus
extensions.exercises: userScripts/scripting, storage, content script style injection
extensions.expectation: an installed user style changes a computed style on the target page

extensions.name: React Developer Tools
extensions.expectation: known-unsupported canary: the devtools page iframe is never created, so the test asserts the current broken behaviour and fails the day it starts working
